why: Budgets sit only on figures the harness measures exactly. jsdom has no layout, paint or compositor, so its millisecond is not a browser's; a threshold on mount or update time would encode jsdom's cost as Modyra's and fail on a faster machine's noise rather than on a regression.

nodesPerField.why: Exact and flat from 100 to 2000 fields, so it is the figure that predicts a large form. 23 is ~1.25x: a legitimate wrapper or two per field passes, an extra nesting level across the catalogue does not.

leakedAfterUnmount.why: Not a multiple of anything. A node surviving unmount is a defect, and 'some leak' is not a budget. Counted on <body>, not the host, so a portalled overlay is included.

churnLeftInBody.why: Same rule over 20 mount/unmount cycles, which is where a per-cycle leak accumulates into something visible and a single teardown shows nothing.

recorded_not_gated.why: Reported every run so a change is visible, gated on nothing. Mount is superlinear above ~500 fields (2.6x cost for 2x fields) and whether that is the engine or jsdom's own DOM construction cannot be separated without a browser harness.

not_measured.inputLatency: no layout, no paint, no compositor
not_measured.listenersAfterDestroy: jsdom exposes no listener registry; post-unmount DOM stands in for the part of the question it can answer
